Dance rattle. Consists of a leather strap knotted closed at one point; multiple goat or antelope hooves are attached to the strap with twisted fibre sting. Worn by men on the arm or leg.

Feather ornament. Tip of two ostrich feathers layered together, the back feather is pink, dyed from local clay. The front feather is black. Bound together as the stems with plant fibre.

garment.title: Decorative element from a girl's apron, made of square ostrich eggshell and brown spherical beads laced together with a strip of hide.

household.title: Cup, made of half a gourd and used by women for drinking. The gourd is decorated with rings of geometric patterns, filled with black pigment. There is a small perforation at the stem of the gourd, through which a small loop of hide.
Half gourd used by men for drinking milk. The gourd is decorated with geometric grooves in a checkerboard pattern. There is a small perforation at the stem, through which is a fibre loop.
Iron razor blade. Roughly triangular with loop at the point.

Spoon made of horn for porridge matama and mwele. The spoon has a large bowl, and short handle with a circular cross-section. There is a perforation at the end of the hole, with a loop of hide or sinew tied through. The bowl has a split in it, which has a contemporary repair made with hide or sinew stitches.

arms.title: Bleeding arrow with a wooden shaft and metal head. The head is rounded and attached to the shaft possibly with hide. The fletchings have come away and are missing.

Nyetubot. Short stabbing spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The spearhead is long and leaf shaped with a midrib; split socket. The shaft is short with a circular cross-section and rounded terminal; the shaft is bound in thin strips of woven hide, with a small attachment loop approximately halfway down.

Throwing spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is leaf shaped with a prominent midrib; long split socket; part of the socket has come away and is missing. The shaft has a circular cross-section, and terminates with a metal ferrule.

Throwing spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is leaf shaped with a midrib; split socket with a circular cross-section. The shaft has a circular cross-section and terminates with a metal ferrule. There is a ring of hide around the shaft near the ferrule.
Spearhead from a throwing spear. The blade is leaf shaped with a prominent midrib. The socket is long and split, with a circular cross-section. Shaft is 1922.1253.2.

Throwing spear with a wooden shaft and metal spearhead. The blade is leaf shaped with a prominent midrib; split socket. The shaft has a circular cross-section, and terminates with a metal ferrule tapering to a point. There is a ring of hide around the ferrule, about halfway down.
Wooden shaft of a throwing spear; the spearhead end tapers to a point. The shaft has a circular cross-section with natural knots present. Spearhead is 1922.1253.1.
